business: Foley Eileen M., Lawyer (E. Foley Firm)
summary: The Law Office of Eileen M. Foley, Esq., LLC is a solo matrimonial/family-law practice in East Brunswick, NJ, run by an attorney admitted in 1989 who says every matter is handled start to finish by her. Clients reach the firm only by phone, email or fax - the website has no form, no scheduler and no tel: link, and the HTTPS version fails on a self-signed certificate. The Google profile is unrated with zero reviews, while independent directories hold only two client reviews (one 5-star from 2017, one 1-star from 2022).

facts.fact: Office address is 330 Milltown Road, Suite W21, East Brunswick, NJ 08816; phone 732-360-8116; fax 732-353-6879; email efoley@efoleyfirm.com.

Practice is described as dedicated to family/matrimonial law since 1990, serving Middlesex, Monmouth, Mercer and Somerset counties and named towns including North Brunswick, Edison, Metuchen, South Brunswick, Monroe, South River, Old Bridge, Milltown and Piscataway.

Listed practice areas: divorce litigation, child custody/parenting time, child support, alimony, child relocation, DCP&P litigation, domestic violence, FD litigation, grandparent visitation, guardianship, juvenile criminal law, post-judgment applications, pre-nuptial and separation/settlement agreements, step-parent adoption.
The site says a client's matter 'will be handled start to finish by Ms. Foley' and that most clients arrive by referral from current or former clients.

Attorney is a 1989 University of Dayton School of Law JD, admitted to the NJ bar in 1989, sits on the Middlesex County Early Settlement Panel and has served on the Middlesex County District VIII Ethics Committee since 2005.
Firm advertises free 15-minute telephone consultations and an in-office consultation fee that is credited against the first legal bill.

Google Business Profile 'Eileen M. Foley, Esq.' is categorised 'Family law attorney' at 330 Milltown Rd W21, lists website efoleyfirm.com and phone (732) 360-8116, shows hours Mon-Fri 9 AM-5 PM and closed Saturday and Sunday, and notes 'Located in: Marc A. Kane, CPA'.

The same Google profile carries no star rating and no reviews (only a 'Write a review' prompt), no owner photos, and attributes 'Onsite services', 'Online appointments', 'Appointment required/recommended', restroom, wheelchair accessible parking lot and restroom.
Eileen Foley is listed as the Middlesex County Bar Association's 2024 Pro Bono Award recipient.
Lawyers.com/Martindale-Hubbell show an overall 3.0 from 2 client reviews with a 4.5 peer review, the title 'Partner', and a stale North Brunswick address ('1 Unknown, North Brunswick, NJ 08902').

Avvo shows 'not yet reviewed', a 6.5 profile rating, an hourly rate of $350, and an address at Borrus, Goldin, Foley, Vignuolo, Hyman & Stahl, PC, 2875 Route 1, North Brunswick - inconsistent with the East Brunswick office on her own site.
Yelp has no listing for the firm - a Yelp search for the practice returns only unrelated East Brunswick law firms and an 'add business' prompt.
The site's blog contains a single post, on the child support law effective February 1, 2017.

operations_signals: Customer front door is a phone number and a mailto link printed as plain text: page HTML contains zero tel: links and zero <form> elements, so a mobile visitor can neither tap to call nor submit an enquiry (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)

Google profile claims 'Online appointments' and 'Appointment required/recommended', but the website has no scheduler or booking widget of any kind - the only path is to call or email (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Eileen+Foley+lawyer+East+Brunswick+NJ)

Published hours are Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM with Saturday and Sunday closed; there is no after-hours line, answering service or chat listed, so evening and weekend enquiries have no recorded path (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Eileen+Foley+lawyer+East+Brunswick+NJ)

Intake is preceded by a free 15-minute phone consultation, i.e. a live screening call by the attorney before any in-office consultation is booked; a testimonial says she 'made time in her schedule' to see a client (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/consultation.html)
No client portal, document upload, payment link or e-signature mention anywhere on the site; the only transaction-adjacent channel is fax at 732-353-6879 (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)
A client testimonial thanks Foley 'and her assistant', indicating at least one support staff member handling client contact alongside the solo attorney (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/testimonials.html)
hiring_signals: No current or recent job postings for the firm were found on Indeed, LinkedIn or general web search as of 2026-11-13; searches for a legal assistant/paralegal role returned only other Middlesex County firms (https://www.indeed.com/jobs?l=Middlesex+County%2C+NJ&q=legal+assistant)
The site has no careers, employment or 'join us' page in its navigation (Home, About, Blog, Consultation/Retainer, Testimonials, Contact) (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)
review_themes: Very low independent review volume: zero Google reviews on a profile that exists, and only two client reviews on Lawyers.com, so the visible average (3.0) rests on a 2017 five-star and a 2022 one-star (https://www.lawyers.com/north-brunswick/new-jersey/eileen-mary-foley-1110997-a/)

Positive review and site testimonial praise responsiveness, strategic 'toughness' with opposing counsel, and a pleasant office staff (https://www.lawyers.com/north-brunswick/new-jersey/eileen-mary-foley-1110997-a/)

The single negative review (April 2022) comes from a litigant whose case she was appointed to as a parenting-time coordinator, complaining about tone and hourly cost - i.e. a court-appointed role, not a retained client; value-for-money scored 3.0 across the two reviews (https://www.lawyers.com/north-brunswick/new-jersey/eileen-mary-foley-1110997-a/)

There are no public reviews about missed calls, billing errors, scheduling or delays; the recurring friction theme is price and hourly billing (https://www.lawyers.com/north-brunswick/new-jersey/eileen-mary-foley-1110997-a/)

Firm-published testimonials (five on the site) emphasise referral origin, settlement focus and keeping cases on track - they are firm-curated, not independent (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/testimonials.html)
tech_footprint: Static HTML site on an old Skeleton-style 16-column template derived from a purchased theme ('Bound'), still loading jQuery 1.7.2 plus a long list of 2000s-era plugins (flexslider, prettyPhoto, jquery.tweet, jflickrfeed, nicescroll) (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)

HTTPS is broken: https://www.efoleyfirm.com/ returns net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID (self-signed certificate), and programmatic fetches fail certificate verification; the site is reachable only over plain HTTP (https://www.efoleyfirm.com/)

On-page SEO is thin: <meta name="description"> is empty, there is no JSON-LD/schema markup, the title names divorce/family law and the counties but not East Brunswick, and leftover commented-out template slider code ('Welcome to Bound') remains in the HTML (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)
Blog is a WordPress install at efoleyfirm.com/blog/ with a single 2017 post, effectively abandoned (http://efoleyfirm.com/blog/)

Only third-party embeds are a Google Maps iframe on the contact page and a Facebook page icon in the header - no chat widget, CRM, booking tool, review widget or analytics tag visible in the markup (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)
Site was built by Pressing Issues Web Design, credited in the footer (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)

Directory footprint is inconsistent: Lawyers.com/Martindale show a North Brunswick '1 Unknown' address, Avvo shows a different North Brunswick firm's address, and Yelp has no listing - while Google shows the East Brunswick suite (https://www.avvo.com/attorneys/08902-nj-eileen-foley-1606317.html)
growth_signals: Named Middlesex County Bar Association 2024 Pro Bono Attorney of the Year, honoured at the MCBA's Annual Practice Area Awards Dinner in March 2024 (source: MCBA award-winner list) (https://anderlarango.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/MCBA-Practice-Area-Award-Winners-Middlesex-County-Bar-Association.pdf)
Positioning is deliberately small and referral-fed - 'quality overrides quantity', most clients by referral - rather than volume growth (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)

No evidence of new offices, new hires, added practice areas or marketing investment: the newest content on the site is from 2017 and the design/scripts date from the same era (http://efoleyfirm.com/blog/)
physical_signals: Single office in Suite W21 at 330 Milltown Road, East Brunswick - a suite number in a multi-tenant professional office building rather than a standalone office (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)

Google places the practice 'Located in: Marc A. Kane, CPA', i.e. at another professional practice's address suite, consistent with a shared/serviced office arrangement (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Eileen+Foley+lawyer+East+Brunswick+NJ)

No interior or exterior photos at all on the Google profile ('Add photos & videos' only), so waiting area, conference room and signage are undocumented publicly (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Eileen+Foley+lawyer+East+Brunswick+NJ)
Physical footprint is one attorney plus at least one assistant; no published headcount, square footage or second location on the site or in directories (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/about.html)

Service area is stated as Middlesex, Monmouth, Mercer and Somerset counties with appearances in Middlesex County Family Court (Early Settlement Panel), so work is court- and office-based rather than a retail storefront (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/about.html)
decision_maker: Eileen M. Foley, Esq. - owner and sole attorney of The Law Office of Eileen M. Foley, Esq., LLC (named on the firm's home, about and contact pages: http://www.efoleyfirm.com/about.html)

inferences.inference: Inbound enquiries outside 9-5 weekdays are probably lost or delayed.
inferences.reasoning: The only channels are a phone number and email; there is no form, chat, answering service, scheduler or after-hours message path, and the sole attorney is in court or with clients during the day (per the Early Settlement Panel and litigation practice described on the site).

inferences.inference: The 'Online appointments' attribute on the Google profile is aspirational, not functional.
inferences.reasoning: Google lists online appointments and 'appointment required', but the website contains no booking widget, scheduler link or form (verified in the page HTML), so a visitor or agent following that attribute hits a dead end.

inferences.inference: Review generation is the largest visible demand-side gap relative to tenure.
inferences.reasoning: Decades of practice and a 2024 county bar award, yet zero Google reviews and only two Lawyers.com client reviews, one of which is a 1-star from a court-appointed role - so the public average understates retained-client sentiment.

inferences.inference: The single 1-star review will keep dragging the average because the sample is so small.
inferences.reasoning: With only two client reviews, the 2022 one-star pulls the displayed average to 3.0; a routine request-to-review process would quickly dilute it.

inferences.inference: Whoever answers the phone is the de facto intake system, most likely the assistant credited in a testimonial.
inferences.reasoning: The site promises the attorney handles matters start to finish, and a testimonial thanks 'her assistant'; with one attorney and one assistant there is no dedicated intake or billing function, which is where repetitive coordination work (screening, conflict checks, engagement letters, retainer billing, calendar management) sits.

inferences.inference: Stale directory data (North Brunswick address on Avvo/Lawyers.com, a different firm name on Avvo) risks mis-routing both humans and AI assistants.
inferences.reasoning: Three directories disagree with the firm's own contact page and the Google profile; an assistant answering 'where is this lawyer' from an old listing would send a client to the wrong town.

inferences.inference: No marketing vendor or web maintenance has been engaged since roughly 2017.
inferences.reasoning: The blog stops in February 2017, the site still runs jQuery 1.7.2 and a 2010s-era template, the meta description is empty, no analytics or schema are present, and HTTPS has lapsed to a self-signed certificate - none of which survive routine maintenance.

data_gaps: Phone-width (390px) rendering could not be observed: this research browser blocks plain-HTTP navigation (ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT) and the HTTPS copy fails certificate validation, so mobile layout was assessed from markup only (viewport meta is present; zero tel: links; zero forms).

The MCBA award page (https://www.mcbalaw.com/page/mcba_probono_award_2024) returned HTTP 403, so the secondary claims 'opened her solo practice in 2016' and 'about 20 years of pro bono work for Central Jersey Legal Services' could not be verified firsthand; only her place on the 2024 Pro Bono Award recipient list was confirmed via a third-party copy of the MCBA list.
No job postings of any kind were found for the firm, so headcount beyond 'attorney + at least one assistant' is unknown.
Google review text could not be read because the profile has zero reviews; Yelp has no listing; the firm's Facebook page is JavaScript/login-walled and was not reviewed.
No published fee schedule, retainer amounts, client counts, revenue or square footage; the $350/hour figure comes from a third-party Avvo profile and may be out of date.
No local news coverage of the firm beyond the bar-association award; no public health, licensing or permit records apply to this practice type.
